patch.summary: Is Kit worth it? Kit (formerly ConvertKit) is a creator-first email marketing platform for newsletters, visual automations, landing pages/forms, and digital product selling. Pricing is subscriber-tiered: Newsletter free (limited automations), Creator from list price and Pro fr…. Strong when Creators and newsletter publishers monetizing an audience. Weak when Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro.

blocks.body: Kit earns a yes only when researched fit beats researched limits — not when the brand is familiar.

sections.heading: Kit: buy when the operating loop matches
sections.body:
Evaluator thesis: Commit when your weekly work needs email campaigns and Creators and newsletter publishers monetizing an audience holds. Counter-signal: Walk when Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro would block go-live.

Capability hinge for this product: email campaigns; newsletter builder; email templates; drag drop editor.

Integrations in research: WordPress, Shopify, Stripe.

Paid tiers that usually matter in evaluation: Creator, Pro.

sections.heading: Who Kit is worth it for — and who should avoid it
sections.body:
Worth it for: Choose Kit when creator/newsletter email with landing pages and monetization is the primary job (including ConvertKit migrations)..

Avoid if: Compare Flodesk for design-led creator email, Beehiiv for newsletter growth platforms, MailerLite for simpler free-tier SMB email, and Omnisend/Klaviyo for ecommerce..

If avoid signals dominate, start the alternative path with MailerLite on the same job-to-be-done.

sections.heading: Kit price/value and next evaluation step
sections.body:
Prove one real workflow on the documented free/trial path before arguing for Creator.

Tradeoff to accept consciously: Campaign/automation depth vs design simplicity.

Next step: run email campaigns end-to-end, then decide.
